instruction.name: xvmod.hu
instruction.description: Compute the remainder of each unsigned 16-bit element in `a` divided by the corresponding element in `b`.

experiments.name: operand dependency chain
experiments.init: li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr0, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr1, $r4; li.d $r4, 1; xvreplgr2vr.b $xr2, $r4

latencies.notes: xj -> result chain. Data-dependent: latency = 5 + 6*4 + 16*quotient_bits/16 = 29 + 4*floor(bits/4) for a 16-bit element. Min 17 with a zero dividend, max 45 at a full 16-bit unsigned quotient. LSX and LASX are identical for every element width although LASX carries twice the lanes, so the lanes (and both 128-bit halves) are refined in parallel and only the element width sets the per-bit rate. It divides magnitudes, so the sign of the operands does not change the timing, and it skips trailing zero digits (a quotient of 2^40 still costs 11 cycles). Measured with divisor 1, where the quotient equals the dividend, so the chain holds its operand constant and needs no helper. The remainder comes from the same divider.

throughput.notes: Range over the same pairs: min CPI 7.50 at 0/65535, max CPI 23.50 at 65535/1. Sample uses 1/1.

notes: LASX variable-latency integer divide/modulo. Latency uses an element-0 reset helper; throughput uses 8 independent lanes. Ranges cover positive operands including powers of two and max values. Both vector sources are recorded separately; they share the same result path where the hardware is symmetric.
